title: The engagement post that rendered on neither screen
relationToF053F116: NONE. Surfaced during the RoutedRecord producer/consumer trace and deliberately not absorbed into that task. This is a content-contract defect, not an identity one, and it neither advances nor blocks F116/F053.

canonicalField.determinedFrom: the producer chain, not naming preference
evidence: prisma/schema.prisma:2465 — `model Post { ... text String ... }`. The domain field is `text`. There is no `body` column.
aura_final:lib/features/feed/domain/post.dart:182 — the client's OWN canonical post model already reads `json['text']`, so the client was disagreeing with itself, not only with the server.
canonicalField.isBodyADistinctConcept: NO, not for posts. `body` does appear in the correspondence family (`pickString(message, const ['body','text','content'])` in thread_composer and thread_message_tile) but that reads a correspondence MESSAGE, a different entity in a different domain. No post producer anywhere emits `body`. There is no semantic collision to preserve and nothing was collapsed.

beforeAfter.producerBefore: post.text — CORRECT, and unchanged. The producer was never the defective side.
beforeAfter.producerAfter: post.text — unchanged. No backend source file was modified; only its spec gained assertions.
beforeAfter.consumerBefore: `postBody: _opt(postRaw, ['body']) ?? _opt(m, ['postBody'])` — two keys, neither of which the producer has ever emitted.

rootCause.how: The model was written against an assumed response shape when the engagement workspace was first wired (d615d4f). A later pass, 3dac187 'align engagement repository and models with live API response shape', corrected four real mismatches against the live API — `records` vs `data`, `record` vs `data`, `needsResponse` vs `pending`, and `post.id` vs a top-level `postId` — and did not catch this one.
rootCause.whyItSurvived: Every consumer guards the content with `if ((record.postBody ?? '').trim().isNotEmpty)`. A wrong key therefore did not throw, did not warn, and did not render a placeholder — the post simply was not there. The failure mode of a missing contract field is indistinguishable from a post with no text, which is exactly why an alignment pass looking for visible breakage walked past it.
rootCause.generalShape: A nullable field read through a key nobody sends, consumed behind an emptiness guard, is invisible. The other three fixed in 3dac187 all had visible symptoms (empty list, empty detail, dead button).

sameClassDefectsFoundInTheSameParse.before: `readDate(m['createdAt'])` — a TOP-LEVEL key the DTO does not emit.
sameClassDefectsFoundInTheSameParse.userVisible: YES — both screens render it with `formatRelative` immediately after the author's name, so both bylines were dateless.
sameClassDefectsFoundInTheSameParse.semanticCare: The DTO carries two timestamps that are genuinely different facts: `routedAt` (when the post reached this institution) and `post.createdAt` (when the person wrote it). They were NOT collapsed. Render position decided it: the value sits in the same row as the author's name on both screens, which is a byline, so it is the post's own time. `routedAt` remains unconsumed and available if a queue-age display is ever wanted.

sameClassDefectsFoundInTheSameParse.userVisible: NO — every consumer uses the route parameter `widget.institutionId`, never `record.institutionId`.
sameClassDefectsFoundInTheSameParse.why: The producer omits it deliberately: the existing backend spec asserts `expect((record as any).institutionId).toBeUndefined()` under the heading 'without exposing participationId or institutionId'. A field that is always empty by contract is the same trap that produced this defect, so it was removed rather than left for someone to trust.

sameClassDefectsFoundInTheSameParse.before: `readDate(m['updatedAt'])` — not on the DTO at all.

compatibilityAlias.why: A transitional read is only justified when deployed producer versions genuinely differ. They do not: no producer, in any version, has ever emitted `body` on this contract. `body ?? text` would have preserved the appearance of a dual contract where only one has ever existed, and would have made the mismatch permanently invisible instead of fixed.

affectedSurfaces.engagementListScreen: Renders the post content truncated — `maxLines: 3`, ellipsis overflow — followed by the author byline and the post time. Now populated.
affectedSurfaces.engagementDetailScreen: Renders the full post content, then the same byline and time. Now populated.
affectedSurfaces.presentationDifferencePreserved: The list truncates and the detail does not. That is a deliberate presentation difference and is untouched; what they now share is the SOURCE.

otherConsumers.searched: All references to RoutedRecord across lib/ and test/.
found: engagement_repository.dart — constructs RoutedRecord for both list() and getDetail()
engagement_providers.dart — list, detail and summary providers
otherConsumers.stale: No consumer outside those two screens read the content or timestamp fields. `EngagementSummary` is a separate DTO and was already aligned by 3dac187 (`needsResponse`).
otherConsumers.fixturesEncodingEitherField: None existed — the engagement feature had no tests before this pass, which is the second reason the defect survived.

added: aura_final:test/institutions/engagement_content_contract_test.dart — 5 tests. Parses the exact producer shape; asserts a payload carrying ONLY the old `body` key does NOT resolve (so reintroducing a tolerant alias fails); asserts a genuinely null post stays null rather than becoming an empty string; asserts the byline timestamp is `post.createdAt` and explicitly NOT `routedAt`.

aura_final:test/institutions/engagement_screens_render_content_test.dart — 3 widget tests driving the REAL list and detail screens with the real producer payload. Model tests alone would not have caught this: the defect was invisible precisely because the screens guard on emptiness, so the proof has to be that the text is on the screen.

aura-backend:institution-engagement.spec.ts — 2 tests. Pins that the DTO exposes content as `text` and emits no `body` alias, and that `post.createdAt` and `routedAt` remain separate values with no top-level `createdAt`.
tests.seededProof: Reverting the client read to `['body']` fails 4 of the new tests across both files, including both screen-render tests. Restoring returns them to green. The wrong-field assumption cannot return quietly the way it arrived.
tests.adjusted: routed_record_actor_domain_test.dart — dropped its `institutionId` assertion, since the field was removed as always-empty-by-contract.

scope.backendSourceChanged: NO — the producer was already correct. Only its spec gained assertions.
scope.meetings: UNTOUCHED — 52 meetings tests pass, verified after the change.

verification.identityGate: PASS — 16 files / 28 sites surface, 1 file / 7 sites typed-person, unchanged by this repair

findingEffects: NONE. F053, F116, F051, F052 and F054-F057 are all unaffected; this defect was never an identity defect and is recorded as unrelated.
nextFrontier: Unchanged and untouched by this repair: CO-RC-C7-005 Phase 5 legacy retirement, which is the only thing that discharges the 15 retirement-owned person-identity sites.
